tasks.title: Isolate the git-core signing-failure tests from host Git configuration
tasks.description: Owner request of 2026-09-30 (docs/development/HANDOFF.md, Next). Queued in docs/development/queue-2026-09-30.json, a self-contained queue with no dependency into tasks.json. Two git-core integration tests fail in a plain `cargo test` on a host whose global Git configuration sets `commit.gpgSign` and `tag.gpgSign` true, `gpg.format=ssh` and a `user.signingKey`, as the Ubuntu GNOME 50 host's does. The planner reproduced both on 2026-09-30 at ca7b826 with `cargo test --locked -p gitturtle-core --no-fail-fast` outside the gate's isolation: `annotation_inspection_preserves_message_and_never_bypasses_signing` (crates/git-core/tests/tags_ignore.rs:110, the tag is created) and `configured_signing_failure_is_reported_instead_of_creating_unsigned_commit` (crates/git-core/tests/workflow.rs:584, `unwrap_err` on an `Ok`: the commit is created, signed). Each sets only `gpg.program=/usr/bin/false` in the fixture's local configuration (tags_ignore.rs:104, workflow.rs:578), so the inherited `gpg.format=ssh` sends signing to `gpg.ssh.program` and the host's key, and the signer the test means to fail succeeds. Both pass under `scripts/gate.py`, whose test stages set `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and an empty `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` (gitturtle-gates skill). The gates skill says to isolate such a test in the test itself. Here the product spawns Git through `GitRepository::execute`, and its write path reads the user's global configuration on purpose (signing, hooks, identity; root AGENTS.md), so a fixture `Command`'s environment (signing.rs:54-72, repository.rs:39-40) cannot reach it. Pin in each fixture's repository-local configuration every key the assertion depends on, the signing format and the program for it, as signing.rs does for its whole setup. Product code does not change. This task comes first because it also unblocks unattended runs on this host: the controller's workspace-tests gate runs plain `cargo test --locked --workspace` in the caller's environment (scripts/agent_loop/runner.py `gates`), so every Rust candidate's gate is red here until these tests are isolated.

acceptance.description: Under a temporary global configuration (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` naming a file in a temporary directory) that sets `commit.gpgSign` and `tag.gpgSign` true, `gpg.format` ssh, a `user.signingKey` and a `gpg.ssh.program` fixture script that writes a non-empty signature, both named tests fail on origin/main and pass after the change. The pull request records the commands and the file's contents; no real key is used.

On a host whose own global configuration sets those keys, plain `cargo test --locked -p gitturtle-core` passes without the gate's isolation. The whole git-core suite is also run under the temporary configuration above, and the pull request names any other test it finds host-dependent, isolated the same way.
No file under crates/git-core/src changes. Each test keeps every assertion it has on origin/main: a failing configured signer makes the write fail and creates no tag or commit.
`python3 scripts/gate.py fast` passes, and `cargo test --locked -p gitturtle-core` and `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

tasks.title: Send native-QA input through Mutter RemoteDesktop
tasks.description: Owner request of 2026-09-29. On GNOME hosts whose XWayland runs with `-enable-ei-portal` (the Ubuntu 26.04 GNOME 50 host), XTest goes through the RemoteDesktop portal, whose "Allow Remote Interaction" prompt swallows keys, so `scripts/native_qa` (XTest through python-xlib, x11.py) cannot drive the app there. The last session's local drivers (`.local/recapture-2026-09-29/tools/mutter_input.py`, a `MutterDriver(x11.Driver)` over `org.gnome.Mutter.RemoteDesktop`, and `qaflow.py`'s focus-checked flow) are the working reference: pointer anchored at the bottom-right corner, monitor scale 1.0, keys only while X focus is on the app, and under Mutter the first wheel click of each batch is dropped. Port that backend into scripts/native_qa: `launch --input mutter`, the default where XWayland's command line has `-enable-ei-portal` if that is detectable. portal.py also finds the FileChooser when Nautilus hosts it (AT-SPI application `org.gnome.Nautilus`), matched by exact dialog title only ("Open File", "Save File"). Keep the guards: keys only with verified X focus on the app, and dialog keys only while a widget inside the dialog holds focus. Never XTest on such a host. Queued in docs/development/queue-2026-09-30.json as well, since the controller's reviewers can run scripts/native_qa's tests and its tooling profile gates them: the `.local/` reference drivers named above exist only in the source checkout the run was started from, not in an attempt clone, so read them there without writing.

acceptance.description: `qa.py launch` accepts `--input mutter` (and `xtest`), and selects mutter by default when XWayland's command line has `-enable-ei-portal`; unit tests cover the selection from a fixture process list and refuse XTest on such a host.

Unit tests with a fake D-Bus session and fake X focus show that keys are refused unless X focus is on the app's window, dialog keys are refused unless a widget inside the matched dialog holds focus, and the first wheel click of a batch is compensated.
portal.py finds a FileChooser hosted by `org.gnome.Nautilus` by exact title ("Open File" or "Save File") and ignores other Nautilus windows, covered by unit tests over a fake AT-SPI tree.

scripts/native_qa/README.md documents the backend, its default, the guards and the known Mutter quirks; `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/native_qa -t scripts -p 'test_*.py'` passes without a display.

tasks.title: Keep the Reflog lists and message whole when an entry is selected
tasks.description: Owner request of 2026-09-30, from docs/validation.md "September 29 whole focus ring in Tags and Reflog" (found on the way). The message editor collapses to its two borders, so its first line paints over "Create a new branch at this commit…". The dialog growing to its height bound is expected. The content (crates/app/src/reflog.rs:282, `reflog-browser-content`, a `flex_col` with `max_h(px(590.).min(body_height) + room)` and `overflow_y_scroll`) holds four children: the entry list's `min_h_0()` wrapper around `reflog-list` (:289), the metadata (:300), the read-only message editor (:301, `h(px(110.))`) and `reflog-commit-files` (:302, `max_h(px(110.))`). Put new frames under docs/evidence/reflog-selected/; the #99 frames stay that build's record of the defect. Depends on `refresh-cw-icon` for scheduling only: one native candidate at a time.

tasks.description: Owner request and decision of 2026-09-30. It partly reverses #100's "unselected segments stay ghost"; see docs/validation.md "September 30 selected segments like the shared helper" and its design review. Queued in docs/development/queue-2026-09-30.json, a self-contained queue with no dependency into tasks.json. Unselected segments get the kit's ghost at two sites: Settings' density segments (crates/app/src/settings.rs ~2127-2137, `button.ghost()`) and the project hub's mode segments (crates/app/src/projects.rs ~717-725). History's segments use the shared `button()` helper (main.rs:1872), whose unselected look is `appearance::control_button_variant(false)` (appearance.rs:383). The mix causes two faults. First, pressing an unselected segment shows the ghost's translucent pressed fill, which on release flips to `selected_hover` and then `selected`: computed 1.65:1, 1.26:1 and 1.03:1 with a hue change in Midnight, Porcelain and Kanagawa Lotus. Second, in Kanagawa Lotus and One Dark the selected label takes `control_label` while its ghost neighbours keep `text`. Give unselected segments `control_button_variant(false)` at both sites. While the hub is busy every mode keeps the ghost's disabled look (projects.rs `self.unavailable()`). tasks.title: Share one focus-ring room helper that follows the installed ring
tasks.description: Owner request of 2026-09-30: cleanups after #94, #96 and #99. Queued in docs/development/queue-2026-09-30.json, a self-contained queue with no dependency into tasks.json. (1) Four clips keep room for the ring a focused Button draws outside its edge, and each computes that room on its own. The repository tab strip does it at crates/app/src/repository_tabs.rs:1902-1903, `tags::ring_room` at tags.rs:15 and `reflog::ring_room` at reflog.rs:14. Your themes rows use settings.rs:1595 `const ROW_RING_ROOM: Pixels = px(3.)`, while the Settings page reveal for those rows reads the installed ring (settings.rs:1630-1631). Add one helper in appearance.rs, beside `BUTTON_FOCUS_RING` and `painted_button`, that returns the installed `Theme::button_focus_ring`'s gap plus width, and use it at all four sites. ROW_RING_ROOM goes, and the rows' room (settings.rs:1673, 1685-1686, 1790, 1807-1811) follows a non-default ring as the reveal does. Keep `rows_off_boundary` (settings.rs:61) and theme_editor.rs:325 `reveal_focused_row` in step. (2) The Your themes rows' fill layer decides hover with `!cx.has_active_drag() && row.hitbox.is_hovered(window)` (settings.rs:1731). GPUI's own hover styles also skip hover after touch input (gpui-pre 0.3.4 elements/div.rs:3374-3395, `!window.last_input_was_touch()`), but `Window::last_input_was_touch` is `pub(crate)` (window.rs:3010). Derive the same modality without patching GPUI: GPUI sets it from the last `PlatformInput` (window.rs:5220-5222). If that proves impossible, report why. (3) At the default ring (2 px width and 1 px gap, so 3 px) nothing moves. Native evidence: the controller adds the native profile to any app Rust change that can render (scripts/agent_loop/rust_surface.py), so this task needs a native attestation whatever it declares. The change is meant to be pixel-neutral at the installed ring, so the evidence is a same-session compare that finds the four sites identical, not a design pass over new pixels. #99's zero-ring tests proved the same for Tags and Reflog. Touch cannot be exercised natively on this host; the view test covers it. Depends on `segments-unselected-like-history` for scheduling only.

tasks.title: Let Tab leave a focused kit Checkbox, Switch, Radio, Toggle, Link or ColorPicker that turns disabled
tasks.description: Owner request of 2026-09-30, from docs/validation.md "September 30 Tab leaves a focused Button that turns disabled" (Still open). For focus the owner asked for what is absolutely necessary. Queued in docs/development/queue-2026-09-30.json, a self-contained queue with no dependency into tasks.json. gpui-base tracks these controls' focus handles only while enabled: `.when(!disabled, |this| this.track_focus(…))` at vendor/gpui-base/src/checkbox.rs:380, switch.rs:362, radio.rs:219, toggle.rs:188, link.rs:178 and color_picker.rs:760 (the swatch). #102 fixed the same trap for Buttons. Once a focused control leaves the rendered frame, GPUI dispatches keys from the root node, above the kit `Root` context that binds Tab and Shift+Tab (vendor/gpui-component/src/root.rs:24-25), so Tab does nothing until a pointer click. #102's disabled-focus patch (vendor/gpui-component/GITTURTLE-PATCH.md ~109, `src/button/button.rs`) keeps a focused disabled Button's handle in the frame as a target that is not a tab stop. The app's `gpui_kit::component` Checkbox and Switch wrap gpui-base's (vendor/gpui-component/src/checkbox.rs ~245 passes `track_focus` into the base element). App sites that disable one while it can hold focus: Settings' Follow system Switch while the Omarchy card is selected (crates/app/src/settings.rs:2078, `.disabled(desktop_theme)` at :2080, which persists); the diff view's partial-line Checkbox while a stage runs (diff_view.rs:489, :492); the ignore dialog's Checkbox while its plan is prepared (ignore.rs:153); and the profile editor's signing Checkbox while it saves (profiles.rs:563). The Subject column's Checkbox (settings.rs:1051) is always disabled. Apply #102's rule to all six controls in the owner that drops the handle: gpui-base, or gpui-component's wrappers where that is the right site, as it was for #102. Enabled controls and unfocused disabled ones stay as they are, and Tab never lands on a disabled control.
